parts.title: The Whale Goes to Court
parts.subtitle: A remarkable legal drama in the U.S.A.
parts.article:
The Whale Goes to Court
A remarkable legal drama in the U.S.A.
(A) In 1818 a whale became the subject of a controversial court case in New York City. The case involved an old law requiring those who sold fish oil to pay a fee in order to have their barrels inspected by city officials, and certified. However, an oil merchant named Samuel Judd refused to pay the inspection fee on three barrels of oil, claiming that no inspection was necessary because it was whale oil, and whales were not fish. The state disagreed, and so a date was set for a court to decide not a point of law, but the answer to a more fundamental question: is a whale a fish?
 
(B) As simple as that question may appear today, the answer was far from obvious in the early nineteenth century. Indeed, the public debate in New York sparked off by the trial was sensational. At stake was nothing less than what most regarded as the order of nature. According to the commonly accepted scheme of things, if an animal was not a beast or a bird, it was a fish, regardless of whether it breathed air or suckled its young. For as long as anyone could remember, all non-human creatures had been organised according to the categories of birds, beasts and fish. For the average person the answer seemed perfectly obvious: whales swam in the sea and therefore they were fish.
 
(C) Against this traditional framework stood the new Linnaean system of classification, which sought to introduce more scientific values into the classification of living things. Barely half a century old in 1818, the Linnaean system controversially classified whales as mammals because they shared two mammalian characteristics: they were warm-blooded and breathed air.
 
(D) So the trial began in December 1818. Judd’s defence lawyers chose as their star witness one of New York’s most prominent figures, the congressman Samuel Mitchill. Referred to as a ‘living encyclopaedia’ and a ‘walking library’, Mitchill was a renowned natural history lecturer at the college of Physicians and Surgeons who liked to dare his students to test his knowledge of the natural world. ‘Show me the fin, and I will name the fish,’ he boasted. Scientifically, it was an open-and-shut case, and Judd’s defence lawyers believed they only had to do one simple thing to win the trial: insist that it be decided by biology alone. Mitchill seemed fully qualified for this role.
 
(E) But this is where the case becomes interesting, and is the reason why the trial of the whale is not some dusty nineteenth-century obscurity. For rather than debate Mitchill on his area of expertise, lawyers for the New York City fish-oil inspectors chose a different tack. Lead counsel William Sampson turned the trial into a contest between scientific learning and common sense, by asking plain-spoken whalers to make their case before the jury.
 
(F) The crux of Sampson’s case was the trial’s implication with regard to humans, should Judd be found not guilty. Sampson told jury members that if they accepted Mitchill’s testimony on whales, they were obliged to accept a lower place for their own kind in the natural order. As a result, Mitchill’s day in court did not go smoothly, not least because he was forced to acknowledge serious disputes among his peers regarding exactly how to classify biological organisms. Sampson then took aim at Mitchill himself and what he represented: privileged aristocrats from the scientific community who had lost touch with reality. The smooth-talking Sampson then claimed Mitchill’s beliefs had their origin in Europe – something he rightly judged would infuriate the citizens of always-independent New York. This revolutionary new thinking Sampson claimed, was something that honest working New Yorkers could do without. No longer was this a case about barrels of oil but the proper place of scientific knowledge in the U.S.A.
 
(G) Ultimately, what won the case for Samuel Judd were not Mitchill’s scientific arguments, but testimony from a different sphere altogether. In New York’s markets, the merchants implicitly understood that whale oil and fish oil were not the same: whale oil could be used as a fuel for lamps because it could be burned without giving off smoke; fish oil, on the other hand, was nasty, impure stuff used primarily in tanning leather. In the end it was this testimony that led to Judd’s victory.
 
(H) The trial of the whale still has relevance today, when the court of public opinion remains easily swayed by sceptics. The 1818 trial was really about this question: who gets to decide on the place of the natural world in the human world – scientific experts or public opinion? Whether the issue today is the effects of human activity on the climate of this planet, or one of many other contemporary topics, the legacy of Judd’s case continues to be of relevance.

questions.question: An inspection fee on fish oil was introduced in New York in 1818.

analyses.content: 你可能看到第一句有“1818”和“fee”就匆忙选了TRUE，忽略了原文明确说这是一项旧法律。

(A) In 1818 a whale became the subject of a controversial court case in New York City. The case involved an old law requiring those who sold fish oil to pay a fee in order to have their barrels inspected by city officials, and certified.
原文说这项要求对鱼油收费的法律是一项“旧法律（old law）”，而不是题目说的在1818年才“引入（introduced）”的，所以是FALSE。

questions.question: Samuel Judd argued that the inspection fee should exclude whale oil.

analyses.content: 原文明确提到Samuel Judd拒绝支付检查费，因为他主张那是鲸鱼油不需要检查，这和题目说的“应该排除鲸鱼油”完全一致，所以是TRUE。
你可能对“exclude（排除）”这个词的同义替换不够敏感，原文的“no inspection was necessary”其实就是把它排除在外的意思。
However, an oil merchant named Samuel Judd refused to pay the inspection fee on three barrels of oil, claiming that no inspection was necessary because it was whale oil, and whales were not fish.

questions.question: Judd had been in trouble with city officials before the inspection fee disagreement.

analyses.content: 原文只提到了Judd这次因为检查费和官员发生分歧，根本没有提他“之前（before）”有没有惹过麻烦，所以是NOT GIVEN。
你可能会根据他敢于抗拒官员的举动，自己脑补他是个“惯犯”或者以前也惹过事，做题千万不能凭空猜测。

The case involved an old law requiring those who sold fish oil to pay a fee in order to have their barrels inspected by city officials, and certified. However, an oil merchant named Samuel Judd refused to pay the inspection fee on three barrels of oil, claiming that no inspection was necessary because it was whale oil, and whales were not fish.

questions.question: Many New Yorkers were interested in the court case at the time.

analyses.content: 题目里的“interested（感兴趣）”对应原文的“sensational（轰动的）”，如果你不认识sensational这个词，可能会不敢选TRUE。
原文说这场审判在纽约引发的公众辩论是“轰动性的（sensational）”，说明很多纽约人对这个案子很感兴趣，所以是TRUE。
Indeed, the public debate in New York sparked off by the trial was sensational.

questions.question: Traditionally, non-human creatures had been classified in one of three groups.

analyses.content: 原文明确指出，一直以来所有非人类生物都被归类为鸟类、野兽和鱼类这“三个类别（categories）”，和题目的“三组”完全一致，所以是TRUE。
你可能在找“three groups”这个具体的词组，但原文是用列举“birds, beasts and fish”来体现数量“三”的。
For as long as anyone could remember, all non-human creatures had been organised according to the categories of birds, beasts and fish.

questions.question: Generally speaking, ordinary people thought fish were the lowest form of life.

analyses.content: 原文提到了普通人觉得鲸鱼在海里游所以是鱼，但完全没有比较谁是“最低等（lowest）的生命形式”，所以是NOT GIVEN。
看到下文提到了人类在自然秩序中接受“较低的位置”，你可能张冠李戴，把它和普通人对鱼的看法混为一谈了。

For as long as anyone could remember, all non-human creatures had been organised according to the categories of birds, beasts and fish. For the average person the answer seemed perfectly obvious: whales swam in the sea and therefore they were fish.

questions.question: Whales were excluded from the Linnaean system in 1818.

analyses.content: (C) Against this traditional framework stood the new Linnaean system of classification, which sought to introduce more scientific values into the classification of living things. Barely half a century old in 1818, the Linnaean system controversially classified whales as mammals because they shared two mammalian characteristics: they were warm-blooded and breathed air.
你可能看到“controversially（有争议地）”就误以为这个系统不承认或者排除了鲸鱼，其实它只是分类方式有争议而已。
原文明确说林奈系统将鲸鱼归类为哺乳动物，说明它被“包含”在系统里，这跟题目说的被“排除（excluded）”完全相反，所以是FALSE。

groups.contentHtml:
The Trial of December 1818
The Personalities
• Samuel Mitchill worked as a congressman and a .
• The defence wanted Mitchill to present the biology of the case.
• William Sampson called as witnesses in order to appeal to the common sense of the jury.
The Arguments
• Sampson’s case was based on the consequences for humans if Judd won.
• Mitchill admitted that scientists had disputes about classification.
• New Yorkers disliked Mitchill because his ideas came from .
Conclusions
• In the end it was statements from local , not Mitchill’s testimony which helped Judd win.
• Whale oil made a good because it was clean.
• Judd’s case is relevant today, e.g. in the debate about Earth’s .

analyses.content: 原文提到Mitchill既是国会议员（congressman），也是一位著名的自然历史讲师（lecturer），所以填lecturer。
你可能会因为看到“living encyclopaedia”等形容词而分心，忘记去寻找表示具体职业身份的名词。

Judd’s defence lawyers chose as their star witness one of New York’s most prominent figures, the congressman Samuel Mitchill. Referred to as a ‘living encyclopaedia’ and a ‘walking library’, Mitchill was a renowned natural history lecturer at the college of Physicians and Surgeons who liked to dare his students to test his knowledge of the natural world.
原文直接写道，Sampson通过让直言不讳的捕鲸者（whalers）在陪审团面前陈述，把审判变成了科学与常识的较量，所以填whalers。
题目中的“called... as witnesses”对应原文的“asking... to make their case”，如果你没看懂这个动作替换，可能会找不到填什么人。
Lead counsel William Sampson turned the trial into a contest between scientific learning and common sense, by asking plain-spoken whalers to make their case before the jury.
The smooth-talking Sampson then claimed Mitchill’s beliefs had their origin in Europe – something he rightly judged would infuriate the citizens of always-independent New York.
原文指出，Sampson声称Mitchill的信仰起源于欧洲（Europe），这激怒了纽约市民，所以填Europe。
题目用“disliked（不喜欢）”替换了原文的“infuriate（激怒）”，如果你在原文苦苦寻找dislike的原词，就会错过这个答案。
原文说明，最终让Judd赢掉官司的不是科学论证，而是纽约市场上商人们（merchants）的证词，所以填merchants。
你可能直接把28句里的“sphere（领域）”填了进去，但仔细看下文的“this testimony”指代的是具体发出证言的人，也就是merchants。

(G) Ultimately, what won the case for Samuel Judd were not Mitchill’s scientific arguments, but testimony from a different sphere altogether. In New York’s markets, the merchants implicitly understood that whale oil and fish oil were not the same: whale oil could be used as a fuel for lamps because it could be burned without giving off smoke; fish oil, on the other hand, was nasty, impure stuff used primarily in tanning leather. In the end it was this testimony that led to Judd’s victory.
原文说鲸鱼油可以作为灯的燃料（fuel），因为它燃烧时不会冒烟（对应题目的clean），所以填fuel。
题目里的“clean（干净）”是对原文“without giving off smoke（不冒烟）”的总结概括，如果你只在原文找clean，就会卡壳。

In New York’s markets, the merchants implicitly understood that whale oil and fish oil were not the same: whale oil could be used as a fuel for lamps because it could be burned without giving off smoke; fish oil, on the other hand, was nasty, impure stuff used primarily in tanning leather.
原文在结尾提到，无论是今天关于人类活动对这个星球气候（climate）影响的问题，还是其他话题，Judd案的遗产依然具有相关性，所以填climate。
题目中的“Earth's（地球的）”对应原文的“of this planet（这个星球的）”，找到这个修饰关系的替换就能精准锁定climate。
Whether the issue today is the effects of human activity on the climate of this planet, or one of many other contemporary topics, the legacy of Judd’s case continues to be of relevance.
